record.evidence_quote: The highest common factor (HCF) of two numbers is the largest number that is a factor of both. For example, the common factors of 12 and 16 are 1, 2 and 4. The number 4 is the largest number on the list, so it is the highest common factor.
record.content_text: The highest common factor (HCF) of two numbers is the largest number that is a factor of both. For example, the common factors of 12 and 16 are 1, 2 and 4. The number 4 is the largest number on the list, so it is the highest common factor.

record_links.rationale: This definition states that HCF is the largest whole number dividing two or more numbers without a remainder.

record.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple

heading_path.h1: Chapter 2: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple
heading_path.h3: Worked example 2.5: HCF using prime factors

record.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors.

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 60 \\
 \hline
 2 & 30 \\
 \hline
 3 & 15 \\
 \hline
 5 & 5 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}
$$

$$
60=2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 5
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 80 \\
 \hline
 2 & 40 \\
 \hline
 2 & 20 \\
 \hline
 2 & 10 \\
 \hline
 5 & 5 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}
$$

$$
80=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5
$$

Step 2: Identify all the prime factors that are contained in both numbers.

The number 2 appears twice for 80 and 60: $2 \times 2$
The number 3 does not appear for 80
The number 5 appears once for 80 and 60: $5$

Step 3: Multiply the prime factors you identified to get the HCF.

$$
\text{HCF} = 2 \times 2 \times 5 = 20
$$

record.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple

heading_path.h1: Chapter 2: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple
heading_path.h3: Worked example 2.6: HCF using prime factors in index form

record.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors in index form.

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 90 \\
 \hline
 3 & 45 \\
 \hline
 3 & 15 \\
 \hline
 5 & 5 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}
$$

$$
90=2 \times 3^2 \times 5
$$

$$
\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 108 \\
 \hline
 2 & 54 \\
 \hline
 3 & 27 \\
 \hline
 3 & 9 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}
$$

$$
108=2^2 \times 3^3
$$

Step 2: Identify the prime factors that are contained in both numbers, to the lowest index.

The number 2 divided into both 90 and 108. The lowest index both numbers have as a factor is one: $2$
The number 3 divided into both 90 and 108. The lowest index both numbers have as a factor is two: $3^2$

Step 3: Multiply the prime factors you identified to get the HCF.

$$
\text{HCF} = 2 \times 3^2=2 \times 3 \times 3 = 18
$$

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 2.6: Use different methods to find the HCF 1. For the following sets of numbers, find all the factors of each number and then find the HCF. 1. 15 and 80 2. 40 and 64 3. 50 and 70 4. 18, 24 and 32 5. 30, 45 and 75
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 2.6: Use different methods to find the HCF

1. For the following sets of numbers, find all the factors of each number and then find the HCF.

   1. 15 and 80
   2. 40 and 64
   3. 50 and 70
   4. 18, 24 and 32
   5. 30, 45 and 75
record.answer_text:
1. 15 and 80

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 15 = 15 \newline 3 \times 5 = 15 \end{array}
$$
Factors of 15: 1; 3; 5; 15

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 80 = 80 \newline 2 \times 40 = 80 \newline 4 \times 20 = 80 \newline 5 \times 16 = 80 \newline 8 \times 10 = 80 \end{array}
$$
Factors of 80: 1; 2; 4; 5; 8; 10; 16; 20; 40; 80

$\therefore$ HCF = 5

2. 40 and 64

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 40 = 40 \newline 2 \times 20 = 40 \newline 4 \times 10 = 40 \newline 5 \times 8 = 40  \end{array}
$$
Factors of 40: 1; 2; 4; 5; 8; 10; 20; 40

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 64 = 64 \newline 2 \times 32 = 64 \newline 4 \times 16 = 64 \newline 8 \times 8 = 64 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 64: 1; 2; 4; 8; 16; 32; 64

$\therefore$ HCF = 8

3. 50 and 70

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 50 = 50 \newline 2 \times 25 = 50 \newline 5 \times 10 = 50 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 50: 1; 2; 5; 10; 25; 50

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 70 = 70 \newline 2 \times 35 = 70 \newline 5 \times 14 = 70 \newline 7 \times 10 = 70 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 70: 1; 2; 5; 7; 10; 14; 35; 70

$\therefore$ HCF = 10

4. 18, 24 and 32

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 18 = 18 \newline 2 \times 9 = 18 \newline 3 \times 6 = 18 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 18: 1; 2; 3; 6; 9; 18

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 24 = 24 \newline 2 \times 12 = 24 \newline 3 \times 8 = 24 \newline 4 \times 6 = 24 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 24: 1; 2; 3; 4; 6; 8; 12; 24

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 32 = 32 \newline 2 \times 16 = 32 \newline 4 \times 8 = 32 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 32: 1; 2; 4; 8; 16; 32

$\therefore$ HCF = 2

5. 30, 45 and 75

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 30 = 30 \newline 2 \times 15 = 30 \newline 3 \times 10 = 30 \newline 5 \times 6 = 30 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 30: 1; 2; 3; 5; 6; 10; 15; 30

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 45 = 45 \newline 3 \times 15 = 45 \newline 5 \times 9 = 45 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 45: 1; 3; 5; 9; 15; 45

$$
\begin{array}{1} 1 \times 75 = 75 \newline 3 \times 25 = 75 \newline 5 \times 15 = 75 \newline \end{array}
$$
Factors of 75: 1; 3; 5; 15; 25; 75

$\therefore$ HCF = 15

record.prompt_text: Find the HCF and the LCM of 24 and 32.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors in index form.

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 24 \\
 \hline
 2 & 12 \\
 \hline
 2 & 6 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$24=2^3 \times 3$$

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 32 \\
 \hline
 2 & 16 \\
 \hline
 2 & 8 \\
 \hline
 2 & 4 \\
 \hline
 2 & 2 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$32=2^5$$

Step 2: For the HCF, identify the common prime factors to the lowest index. For the LCM, list all the prime factors to the highest index.

| HCF | LCM |
| --- | --- |
| $2^3$ | $2^5\times3$ |
| $2\times2\times2=8$ | $2\times2\times2\times2\times2\times3=96$ |
| Largest number that can divide into 24 and 32 | Smallest number into which 24 and 32 can divide |
